Loss-of-function mutations in FKRP disrupt the essential alpha-dystroglycan glycosylation pathway. This disruption leads to the characteristic congenital muscular dystrophy phenotype in disease A, and the more severe muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy with brain and eye anomalies in disease B, as proper glycosylation is critical for both muscle integrity and brain/eye development.
